InnoPharm Therapeutics - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the InnoPharm Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss InnoPharm Therapeutics's financial results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Doe, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Elena Vasquez, Head of Commercial; and Tom Harris, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of InnoPharm Therapeutics.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. InnoPharm Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the Q2, driven by robust commercial execution on our recently launched CAR-T therapy INP-300 and key regulatory wins that expand our addressable markets. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, focusing on regulatory approvals and label expansions achieved, clinical trial updates including phase progression, data readouts, and regulatory milestones, as well as our broader pipeline momentum that positions us for multi-billion peak sales potential. Before turning to financials, let me highlight our transformative quarter in regulatory momentum. In this high-stakes pharma world where FDA PDUFA dates and EMA timelines define value, we've secured a hat-trick of approvals and expansions unlocking over $2.5 billion in incremental peak sales across immuno-oncology, rare diseases, and cardiometabolics, much like the trajectories of Merck's Keytruda or Novartis' Zolgensma.

First, the U.S. FDA approval of our sNDA for ONCO-101 in first-line non-small cell lung cancer. Our flagship PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, generating substantial U.S. sales from second-line metastatic use, saw the Phase 3 ONCO-LIFT trial with 1,024 patients across 180 global sites demonstrate superior PFS of 14.2 months versus 9.8 months for pembrolizumab alone—a 45% hazard ratio reduction. ORR reached 68%, with Grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events at 22%. This priority review under Breakthrough Therapy Designation catapults ONCO-101 into the $25 billion frontline NSCLC market, forecasting 15-20% U.S. penetration and $1.8 billion in added peak sales by 2028, supported by formulary wins and our ONCO-Select companion diagnostic.

Second, EMA approval for GENE-X in spinal muscular atrophy Type 2 patients under 2 years old, building on our U.S. Type 1 launch. Pooled EXPAND-2 data showed 89% achieving motor milestone gains, with stable transgene expression and low immunogenicity. Europe's $1.2 billion SMA market now sees €350 million in Year 1 revenue potential at €1.8 million pricing, triggering €75 million Takeda milestones.

Third, PMDA approval in Japan for CardioZorb's expansion into NYHA Class II HFrEF, with ZORB-JPN trial data showing 62% LDL-C reduction and 32% lower CV events. Partnering with Daiichi Sankyo targets ¥80 billion peak sales in Japan's ¥500 billion market.

These stem from our Regulatory Velocity Initiative using real-world evidence and AI trial designs, slashing timelines. U.S. drove 75% value, with more expansions like ONCO-101 in MSI-high cancers ahead. We are particularly excited about INP-450, our next-gen bispecific T-cell engager, and its potential to dominate the multiple myeloma market with best-in-class efficacy.

Now, I will turn the call over to Jane Doe, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jane Doe, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid Q2. Revenue for the quarter was $412 million, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by expanded label inclusion for frontline NSCLC on ONCO-101/NVX-101, U.S. net sales of $285 million up 35%, and ex-U.S. at $110 million from Japan and Australia launches.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $85 million, or $0.72 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $112 million, or $0.95 per share.

As we dive deeper into our operating expense analysis, total operating expenses came in at $478 million, up 12% year-over-year from $427 million and 5% sequentially from Q1. This disciplined spending aligns with pipeline priorities amid 8-10% inflation in trial costs and talent pressures in biotech hubs. R&D at $312 million, 65% of OpEx and up 18% YoY, ramped for INP-450's Phase 3 ORION-2 trial enrolling 400 patients globally, with $45 million recruitment and $28 million CMC costs, plus $22 million for INP-720 gene therapy in DMD. North America 55%, Europe 30%, Asia-Pacific 15%. AI with Schrödinger reduced timelines 25%, reallocating $15 million. R&D at 180% of sales, below peers.

SG&A at $166 million, up 2% YoY but flat sequentially, post INP-300 launch capturing 8% share in $2.5 billion market. Sales force up 15% to 350 reps added $12 million, marketing $18 million offset by $8 million IT savings. U.S. 70%, Europe $25 million, APAC $10 million. Targeting 5-7% FY OpEx growth below industry 10%, non-GAAP $460 million, path to EBITDA positivity 2026.

Our cash position remains strong at $1.8 billion. On cash flow and balance sheet highlights, we ended Q2 with $1.8 billion in cash equivalents and investments, up 22% YoY, providing a 4.2-year runway. Debt $1.1 billion yields net debt of $400 million at 0.8x leverage. DSO 52 days, inventory 142 days, working capital $650 million. Operating cash flow $520 million up 28%, from $950 million revenues led by NovaCure bispecific. Investing outflows $380 million on R&D capex and tuck-in acquisition; free cash flow $310 million.

On pricing and reimbursement, U.S. 62% of sales sees 52% discounts; NovaLipid WAC $6,200, ASP $4,100 post 4.8% hike. IRA headwinds mitigated by value-based deals, 85% Medicare placement. Europe 28%, Germany premium at 18% rebate, France erosion offset. Japan premium JPY 450,000, China NRDL at 42% discount. Biosimilar defense and outcomes-based contracts sustain 8% price growth.

For Q4 2024 guidance, total revenue $460-485 million, 12-18% sequential growth: NVX-101 $350-370 million, royalties $60-70 million, collaborations $50 million. Gross margins 82-84%. Full-year 2025 $2.05-2.25 billion, 25-35% growth: core sales $1.6-1.75 billion, new products $250-300 million. U.S. 65%, Europe/Asia ramps.

Key upcoming catalysts: Q1 2025 Phase 3 NVX-202 readout in myeloma, 65% ORR; March PDUFA NVX-301 IL-2 in melanoma; Q2 NVX-401 DMD gene therapy; H1 partnerships and biosimilars; manufacturing/AI tech.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $1.65 billion revenue.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Michael Chen, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Jane. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Our pipeline remains the cornerstone, with four programs advancing late-stage and two topline readouts exceeding expectations. Enrollment up 25% YoY.

Flagship BNV-301/INP-450 HER2 ADC for breast/gastric: Phase 3 HERCULES-3 topline met ORR 68% vs 32%, mPFS 15.2 vs 6.8 months. BLA rolling next week, PDUFA Q4 2025; EMA MAA mid-2025; peak $2.5 billion.

BNV-450 CRISPR hemophilia A: Phase 2 HEM-EDIT 52 IU/dL Factor VIII, 97% bleed reduction; Phase 3 dosing started, RMAT designation; $250 million partner upfront.

BNV-720 bispecific NSCLC: Phase 1b ORR 41%, Phase 2 initiated.

BNV-610 DMD ASO: Phase 2 enrollment complete, North Star +4.2 points.

We expect BLA submissions and readouts ahead.

Next, Dr. Lisa Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research, advancing AI-integrated discovery, next-gen ADCs, gene therapies, and bispecifics, with nominations in neurodegeneration and oncology, supporting diversified $15 billion opportunity.

Now I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Elena Vasquez, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Our sales performance this quarter was robust, with prescriptions up 18% YoY to 4.2 million TRx, NRx 22% to 1.8 million. Zepara GLP-1 at 14.2% share, OncoTarget NSCLC 9.5%. Sales force productivity 28.4 Rx/rep/day, 92% HCP reach. ROAS 4.8x, digital 7.1x. Zepara $1.2 billion up 31%, OncoTarget $850 million steady. U.S. 78% sales, Europe 17%, APAC 5% up 45%. Precision Commerce AI boosts NRx 14%.

Finally, Tom Harris will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Harris, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Elena. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. We've scaled Cincinnati and Singapore facilities, reducing API costs 15% via continuous tech, Boulder for 50% ADC capacity, supporting $500 million new streams and global supply chain resilience with CROs like WuXi.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Tom. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the OpEx ramp for INP-450 Phase 3, how should we think about R&D intensity peaking and the Roche partnership impact?

Jane Doe, CFO:
Thanks, David. R&D intensity peaks as Phase 3 de-risks, stabilizing at 55-60% OpEx by 2025 with Roche's $200 million upfront for INP-720 freeing resources. FY growth 5-7%, AI efficiencies key.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, J.P. Morgan:
Great, thanks. For the regulatory wins like ONCO-101 frontline, what's the launch timeline and payer traction?

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Emily, ONCO-101 frontline launch immediate post-PDUFA, with CVS formulary wins and 92% diagnostic sensitivity driving 15% penetration quickly, adding $1.8 billion peak.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim, Morgan Stanley:
On clinicals, BNV-301 BLA details and hemophilia Phase 3 enrollment?

Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Robert, rolling BLA starts CMC next week, clinical Q1 2025, PDUFA Q4 with Priority Review. Hemophilia Phase 3 first patient dosed, on track for 2025 completion, RMAT accelerating.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong, Bank of America:
Thanks. Marketing metrics strong—digital ROAS upside and Zepara Europe reimbursement path?

Elena Vasquez, Head of Commercial:
Lisa, digital 7.1x ROAS from personalization, Zepara Europe NRx 8% now but HTA dossiers target NICE/France approvals Q4, DCP advantage key.

Operator:
Our next question from Mike Patel with Citi.

Mike Patel, Citi:
On cash flow, how does $1.8 billion runway support M&A, and 2025 FCF margins?

Jane Doe, CFO:
Mike, runway to 2028, supports $500M-$1B bolt-ons in rare diseases. 25% FCF margins via BioEfficiency savings.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the Q&A. I'll now turn back to the CEO.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the InnoPharm Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
